record_verbatim.evidence: The harness documents RELAX_CLANG_DIAGNOSTICS=1 as silencing 'three diagnostics that Apple clang enables by default and GNU gcc does not'. Two of the three (-Wno-enum-conversion, -Wno-parentheses-equality) are: both are Clang default-on diagnostics whose GCC analogues are not enabled by -Wall or -Wextra. The third, -Wno-array-bounds, is not a clang-only diagnostic. GCC's -Warray-bounds IS enabled by -Wall, so a construct that trips it trips under both compilers and cannot be a platform artefact. Every one of the 25 sites it was hiding is a real out-of-bounds access, verified by hand against the declaration: tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/tx-cyclic/test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures.c:93 declares `float_t testSignalData[3u] = {0u, 1u, 2u};` and the test indexes it at 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 at lines 381, 382, 420, 421, 431, 432, 442, 443, 453, 454, 464, 465 -- out of bounds by up to 9 elements past a 3-element array. The three sibling files test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_{3,4,5}-temp-sensors.c declare the same `float_t[3]` and index it at 4 through 10. tests/unit/app/driver/can/cbs/tx-cyclic/test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-voltages.c:92 declares `float_t testSignalData[4u]` and indexes it at 6 and 8 at lines 367 and 379. tests/unit/app/engine/diag/cbs/test_diag_cbs_current.c:112-117 writes `diag_kpkDatabaseShim.pTableMsl->cellChargeOvercurrent[BS_NR_OF_STRINGS]` and five siblings into a `uint8_t[1]`, and tests/unit/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg_unit_test.h:124 sets BS_NR_OF_STRINGS to (1u) for the default unit-test build, so the index is 1 into a one-element array -- a genuine off-by-one that looks like a test author intending to exercise the out-of-range string index and instead writing outside the array. The 6 affected tests are: test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_3-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_4-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_5-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-voltages.c and test_diag_cbs_current.c. Raw evidence: the per-test logs under docs/artifacts/.work/verification-env/sil/logs/per-test-*/ carry every diagnostic with file, line and column, and each result record in the sweep JSON carries the diagnostic code set with sites.
record_verbatim.impact: Two things, and the second is the reason the severity is high. First, a build that compiled because this warning was silenced is exactly the failure mode the task forbids: the 6 tests would have been reported as building, and readers of a pass count would reasonably infer that their assertions mean something. They do not. A test that reads and writes up to 9 elements past a 3-element array is not measuring the code under test; it is reading whatever the linker happened to place next, and the value it then asserts on is not the value the fixture nominally set. The counts would have been green and meaningless. Second, the flag's presence contaminated the classification scheme itself. Because -Warray-bounds was suppressed under RELAX_CLANG_DIAGNOSTICS while the primary recorded sweep ran WITHOUT that mode, these 6 tests were recorded as build failures attributed to 'build:strict_diagnostic' -- a class defined as 'Apple-clang-only diagnostic promoted by -Werror' -- which is a false description of a real defect. Any reader who accepted that class name would have closed the finding as a known host-platform artefact. Removing the flag and re-measuring moves them to build:real_defect_out_of_bounds_array_index, where they are visible as what they are.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED, in both halves, and this record was stale in a way that mattered. Its resolution said the flag had been removed and the 6 tests 'remain red and are reported as such' - true when written, no longer true, and reporting it otherwise would have told a reader that six real out-of-bounds accesses were still live when they are not.

HALF ONE, the masking flag. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: the string '-Wno-array-bounds' appears nowhere in sil/run.sh, so the flag is removed and stays removed. This half was already closed when the record was written.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER REVISION OF THIS RESOLUTION, recorded rather than quietly replaced: that revision said the RELAX_CLANG_DIAGNOSTICS list 'now holds exactly two diagnostics, -Wno-enum-conversion and -Wno-parentheses-equality'. That was wrong. It counted only the first two entries in the env-gated block and did not read the whole block. Measured: the block adds SEVEN diagnostics - -Wno-enum-conversion, -Wno-parentheses-equality, -Wno-unknown-warning-option, -Wno-pragma-pack, -Wno-literal-conversion, -Wno-non-literal-null-conversion and -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers - and each carries its own justification comment in sil/run.sh and its own entry in sil/RELAXED-DIAGNOSTICS.md. The list held three entries when this finding was raised; the diagnostic that was removed is the one that caught defects rather than reporting style, and the other six are the ones that satisfy the two-part test this finding established. The wrong count was caught by re-deriving the list programmatically rather than by reading the first two lines, which is the same mistake in miniature as the one this record is about. sil/run.sh's own header comment said 'three diagnostics' and has been brought up to date for the same reason.

HALF TWO, the 6 sites. Closed. All six tests now build and pass: test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_3-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_4-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-temperatures_5-temp-sensors.c, test_can_cbs_tx_f_cell-voltages.c and test_diag_cbs_current.c. The fixes are the one-line-per-site changes this record's own resolution specified, and they are test-fixture changes: the declared sizes were corrected - float_t[3] to float_t[13] in the cell-temperature files, which are indexed up to element 12, and float_t[4] to float_t[9] in the cell-voltage file, which is indexed at 6 and 8 - and test_diag_cbs_current.c now writes element 0 of the BS_NR_OF_STRINGS-indexed arrays instead of element 1 into a one-element array. The build-failure class build:real_defect_out_of_bounds_array_index, which carried 6 tests in the baseline sweep, no longer appears in the classifier output at all.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN. The second harm this record identified was to the evidence rather than to the records - the classification scheme had been describing six real defects as 'build:strict_diagnostic', a class defined as 'Apple-clang-only diagnostic promoted by -Werror', which is a false description. That misclassification is corrected by the sites no longer failing, and the classifier no longer emits that class for them. The general rule this record established - a diagnostic may be silenced in this harness only if it is BOTH Apple-clang-only AND about a construct established to be correct, and a class that exists to explain away a red build must never be able to swallow a real defect - remains in force and is written down in sil/RELAXED-DIAGNOSTICS.md. It is a rule about the harness, not about the product: no product source is involved in this finding, no product behaviour was in question, and the defect was entirely within the test fixtures. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. record_verbatim.root_cause: The flag list was assembled on the reasoning 'this diagnostic fires under -Werror, and it fires on vendored or generated code, so it is a platform nuisance' rather than on the two-part test each flag actually has to pass. -Warray-bounds passes 'it fires' and fails 'it is clang-only', and the second condition is the one that decides whether silencing is legitimate. There is a compounding factor specific to this harness: -Warray-bounds is a diagnostic that CATCHES defects rather than reporting style, so the cost of a false negative is categorically higher than for the other two. The same reasoning error was audited for the remaining flags and is why the list was not simply extended: four further diagnostics that also fire were examined and NOT silenced, for the same reason in different clothes - -Wtautological-pointer-compare (src/app/driver/afe/maxim/common/mxm_17841b.c:707 compares an array member against NULL, always true), -Wmissing-field-initializers and -Wunused-but-set-variable (both -Wall/-Wextra in BOTH compilers), and the `section` attribute error in src/version/version.h:83, which is a hard Mach-O error that no -W flag can suppress and which was deliberately not worked around by overriding the macro. The general rule now enforced is stated in sil/RELAXED-DIAGNOSTICS.md: a diagnostic may be silenced in this harness only if it is BOTH Apple-clang-only AND about a construct established to be correct, and a class that exists to explain away a red build must never be able to swallow a real defect.
